samples.question: This image shows five square panels of the same size standing side by side in one row, each framed in grey and numbered 1 to 5 from left to right. Every panel holds exactly two rings, drawn as thin closed circular outlines, and exactly one small solid black dot. Within a scene all ten rings use the same two sizes, so ring size, ring colour and the amount of ink carry no information. The two rings of a panel never touch and never cross: they are either nested, with the smaller ring lying completely inside the larger one, or set apart side by side with a clear gap between them. A dot is enclosed by a ring when it lies inside that ring's closed outline. Exactly one panel in the image holds a dot that is enclosed by both of its rings at once, which happens only when the rings are nested and the dot lies inside the smaller of them. In each of the other four panels the dot is enclosed by exactly one of the two rings or by neither of them, and in every panel the edge of the dot clears every ring outline by at least 6 pixels, so no dot ever sits on a ring. Whether a panel's rings are nested or set apart, which ring the dot of a losing panel sits in, and where the pair sits inside its panel are all free to vary. Which numbered panel holds the dot that is enclosed by both of its rings? Answer with exactly one of: panel-1, panel-2, panel-3, panel-4, panel-5.
